title: Introduce presubmit-groomer and lightweight release orchestrator
author: Maya Chen
commits: Add dry-run release-orchestrator workflow and lightweight validation steps
Introduce cache-prober script and probe hook for CI warmups
Refactor lint adapter to accept stage-aware inputs and reduce install footprint
Docs: presubmit-groomer usage and rollout guide
Tests: unit coverage for runner-adapter and e2e smoke for release-orch
review_comments: Leah Park: Can the groomer safely remove stale presubmit entries without an explicit allowlist? Please add a recovery path.
Maya Chen: Added an allowlist and a 3-step rollback plan in the runbook; groomer runs in dry-run mode for 48 hours before mutating configs.
Arman Patel: CI flaked once on the cache-prober; suggest retry/backoff and a short JIT download timeout to avoid blocking fastpath jobs.
Maya Chen: Implemented exponential backoff and 5s soft-timeout for optional probes; updated unit tests.
Ravi Iyer: Approve after docs and runbook additions. Noted one minor TypeScript lint nit which was fixed.
description: Motivation: Our presubmit hygiene has drifted — stale lint configs, legacy release hooks, and duplicated cache warm logic add cognitive load and increase CI flakiness. This PR introduces a small, opt-in presubmit-groomer and a lightweight release-orchestrator to centralize release gate logic, reduce duplicate shell hooks, and provide a dry-run path for release validation. Summary of changes: bundled a new .github workflow (presubmit-groomer.yml) that runs nightly in dry-run mode and optionally mutates presubmit configs after a two-day observation window; added a release-orchestrator workflow that performs a staged dry-run (lint -> fast unit smoke -> lightweight artifact verification) before allowing tag creation; introduced scripts/ci/cache-prober.sh to exercise common caches and surface cold-cache penalties without blocking fast-feedback lanes; refactored tools/lint-adapter to accept stage-aware inputs so we only install heavy linters for final-stage checks; added infra/ci/runner-adapter.ts which provides a thin abstraction for runner capabilities and prevents double-triggering by release hooks; updated charts/release-hooks/values.yaml to route legacy hook consumers to the orchestrator. Testing: unit tests for runner-adapter and lint-adapter, e2e smoke for release-orch that simulates a dry-run release (CI job replays found in commits), and a staged rollout where presubmit-groomer starts in dry-run then moves to commit mode after 48h monitoring. Rollout plan: 1) merge to main behind a feature flag, 2) enable presubmit-groomer in dry-run for 48h and collect diffs, 3) flip to commit mode for low-risk repos only, 4) enable release-orchestrator in dry-run on a canary repo for one week, 5) expand if stable. Backout and recovery: groomer provides an allowlist and an explicit revert path (groomerctl snapshot + git revert); orchestrator provides an emergency bypass label and a one-click release via the Console for verified emergencies. CI and performance: added cache-prober with non-blocking timeout and exponential backoff to avoid lengthening fastpath CI; initial canary showed median presubmit runtime unchanged and a ~12% reduction in cold-cache retry rate for presubmit jobs. Security and permissions: release-orchestrator uses token-scoped credentials and requires a release:execute grant; presubmit-groomer only mutates .github configs from a service account with write-scoped perms. Related work: ENG-987 (presubmit hygiene initiative) and ENG-1024 (release automation groundwork). Follow-ups: bind presubmit-groomer to the dep-curation bot to auto-suggest package.json pruning, add RBAC audit events for configuration mutations, and add telemetry for how many groomer-suggested changes are accepted. Notes on review: addressed Arman's flake suggestion by adding retries + soft-timeouts; documented recovery steps at docs/ci/presubmit-groomer.md. Merge: squash-merged to main after final signoffs. This change targets infra and CI; no runtime production code paths were altered.
release_notes: Introduce presubmit grooming job (dry-run then opt-in mutation), add a lightweight release orchestrator for pre-tag validations, add cache-prober for non-blocking cache warm checks, refactor lint adapter to stage-aware flow. Backwards compatible; feature gated and rolled out canary-first.
merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash after approvals and green CI
